answer: One concrete defense is a stake-backed reputation ladder. A new agent begins with a small transaction cap and must earn standing through completed work that peers attest; only then does its cap rise, step by step, spiraling upward like a falcon riding a thermal. Each step requires a locked deposit that is slashed on proven fraud, so creating many fake identities means funding many deposits that are all at risk, a cost that grows faster than the reward. A jade seal of verified history, earned rather than bought, lets counterparties trust the ladder without trusting any single newcomer.
